title: Olkaria: Deadlock Character Sheet

roles.strike: Round 1: How much data-centre power use will Kenyans accept?
Round 2: What will the Government offer instead of a guarantee?
Round 3: What will Kenya's businesses commit to?

briefing: Microsoft and G42 want to build a US$1 billion data centre at Olkaria, Kenya's geothermal steam fields, with a headline capacity of 1 GW. Microsoft president Brad Smith called it the “single biggest step to advance the availability of digital technology”. However, the project is now deadlocked for three reasons. First, President Ruto has said that switching it on would “shut off power for half the country”, and some lines already run above 120% of their design capacity. Second, the Treasury will not sign the anchor-tenant guarantee Microsoft wants, which is a government promise to cover demand for the data centre's capacity. Third, Kenya's whole data-centre market is about 20 MW, so 1 GW would be about 50 times its current size.

Principal Secretary John Tanui says the project is “not failed or withdrawn” but “requires some structuring”, so your party's job is to find that structure. In rounds 1 to 3 one stakeholder sets its terms, and in round 4 Microsoft decides.
steps: The narration sets the scene and names the lead character.
Everyone votes on their phone, and voting ends after 2 minutes or once everyone has voted. The lead class's votes make up half the attack, and the rest of the party's votes make up the other half.

The vote then locks, and the facilitator calls out up to 4 voters, each for a different option, to defend their pick in one breath. A defence the room finds convincing earns a rally strike, which adds 10 damage.
The party then strikes, and the damage shows on the boss number by number.
The debrief shows what each option did, then gives your table one question to argue over.

scoring.text: It measures how well the case's evidence supports the options the party chose. Each boss has 100 HP, and if the party deals less than 180 damage in total, the Deadlock holds.
The whole party casts with the Wizards, and the options score on how well they fit what the party chose in rounds 1 to 3. The option with the most votes decides the ending.
You score your option's evidence weight, plus up to 20 for voting early and 10 when your class leads the round. If you're called out, you also get 10 for answering, or 30 if you win the rally.

rounds.question: Q1. How much data-centre power use will Kenyans accept?
rounds.narration: Olkaria steam fields. The Grid Wyrm coils around the plants that make about 950 MW. President Ruto has told the country that switching on the data centre would mean switching off power for half of it. Some lines already run above 120% of their design capacity. Geothermal expansion here once displaced hundreds of Maasai families. Rogues, this is your strike: what will Kenyans accept?

options.screen: Put households first. The deal waits for new generation, and no data-centre load connects until household and industrial supply is secure.
options.phone: On your phone: Households first, deal waits

options.screen: Accept a first phase of 60 to 100 MW, about 4% of peak demand, on condition that new generation is tied to every expansion.
options.phone: On your phone: Yes to 60 to 100 MW, tied

options.screen: Accept the full 1 GW in return for the jobs, the skills lab and the regional hub.
options.phone: On your phone: Full 1 GW for the hub

options.screen: Accept only with a community deal, which gives Olkaria communities compensation and a share of the benefit before any expansion.
options.phone: On your phone: Community deal first

rounds.factsLabel: Facts in play, the three exhibits on the road to this boss

rounds.question: Q2. What will the Government offer instead of a guarantee?
rounds.narration: Nairobi, outside the Treasury. The Debt Golem is built from the numbers: public debt about 68% of GDP, debt service taking 48.5% of ordinary revenue, the IMF asking that commitments like an anchor-tenant guarantee be counted as debt. In June 2024, protests over the Finance Bill left people dead and the bill withdrawn. In September 2026 the High Court ruled that PPP liabilities need Parliament. Microsoft wants a guarantee. Knights, this is your strike: what does the Government offer?

options.screen: Sign the anchor-tenant guarantee, because the hub is worth the risk.
options.phone: On your phone: Sign the guarantee

options.screen: Offer no guarantee of any kind, so Microsoft either builds on market terms or doesn't build.
options.phone: On your phone: No guarantee, market terms

options.screen: KenGen signs a smaller power and capacity commitment for a 60 MW phase, which stays off the national balance sheet.
options.phone: On your phone: KenGen signs, 60 MW

options.screen: Offer no guarantee and buy services instead. Government services move to the local region under the Cloud Policy, and annual budgets pay for them.
options.phone: On your phone: Government as customer

rounds.factsLabel: Facts in play, the three exhibits on the road to this boss

facts.text: Public debt about 68% of GDP, June 2025
48.5% of ordinary revenue goes to debt service
PPP liabilities need Parliament's approval, September 2026

rounds.question: Q3. What will Kenya's businesses commit to?
rounds.narration: The Fog. Microsoft wants proof that Kenyans will pay before it builds. Kenya's entire data-centre market is about 20 MW; iXAfrica's flagship runs 4.5 MW. The market was worth about US$266 million in 2025 and may reach US$805 million by 2031, still below the project's headline. One survey says 97.5% of online Kenyans use AI; Microsoft's own measure says 8.7% of the population. Oracle, Huawei and Nxtra are already selling. Bards, this is your strike: what do Kenya's businesses put on the table?

options.screen: Safaricom, the banks and the large startups sign letters of intent now. They will move workloads to a Nairobi region if its price and latency beat South Africa's.
options.phone: On your phone: Sign letters of intent

options.screen: Partner with Microsoft. EcoCloud and local developers co-build a 60 MW first phase and sell capacity to Kenyan firms as they migrate.
options.phone: On your phone: Co-build 60 MW with EcoCloud

options.screen: Keep workloads with Oracle at iXAfrica, Huawei and South Africa until Azure's local pricing is known, then compare.
options.phone: On your phone: Wait, compare providers

options.screen: Make no commitments until the innovation lab and training promised in 2024 replace the development centre that is closing.
options.phone: On your phone: Skills lab before contracts

rounds.factsLabel: Facts in play, the three exhibits on the road to this boss

facts.text: Kenya's data-centre market is about 20 MW
Market worth US$266 million in 2025, US$805 million by 2031
97.5% of online Kenyans vs 8.7% of all Kenyans used AI

rounds.question: Q4. What should Microsoft do?
rounds.narration: The Deadlock's core is exposed. Kenya's Treasury will not guarantee demand. The Nairobi development centre is closing. Competitors are building. Microsoft must decide how much risk to take, and when. Wizards, this is your strike, and the whole party casts with you: what should Microsoft do?

options.screen: Build the full 1 GW, take a larger stake and secure dedicated generation.
options.phone: On your phone: Full 1 GW build

options.screen: Build a 24 to 60 MW facility now, then expand in stages as contracts and power arrive.
options.phone: On your phone: Build small, expand later

options.screen: Pause Kenya and put the capital into South Africa, then return when power, finances and demand improve.
options.phone: On your phone: Wait, invest elsewhere

options.screen: Local partners such as EcoCloud build and own the facility, and Microsoft rents Azure capacity there as the anchor tenant.
options.phone: On your phone: Partners build, we rent

facts.text: US$1 billion is 0.6% of Microsoft's FY2027 capex
Microsoft committed US$329 million more to South Africa, April 2026
